title: Sterile Insect Technique
abstract: Area-wide integrated pest management is designed for specific purposes, and an economic evaluation should determine its performance against those purposes. The sterile insect technique is used for eradication, suppression, containment and prevention, each of which has different performance measures. Eradication or suppression of insect pest populations using the sterile insect technique (SIT), together with other area-wide control measures, may require significant initial capital investments to achieve long-term returns in subsequent periods. It may also raise questions about the distribution of benefits or the justification of public or private pest control efforts, given long-term uncertainties about the pest challenge and the potential of new control options. A consistent and transparent evaluation is needed to analyse the benefits and costs of such projects and to demonstrate their value, or in some cases to assess appropriate contributions to the costs by the various stakeholders who gain the benefits. Suppression must be compared with expected losses and costs in alternative conditions without SIT application, either from recent experience prior to implementation of the SIT or with similar areas without SIT treatment. Preventive SIT should reduce the frequency of outbreaks compared with experience prior to the application of the SIT or in similar areas elsewhere without SIT use. This chapter outlines the process of benefit/cost analysis, in which itemized future costs and benefits are compared in terms of present values. It also provides a review and examples of the application of benefit/cost analysis to the SIT. A checklist of benefit/cost analysis inputs and some example benefit/cost outputs are also presented.

narrative:
Short impact summary

Sterile Insect Technique (2021), published by Taylor & Francis, has been cited 382 times — enough that OpenAlex puts it in the top 1% of works in its field and year. Beyond that, it has been downloaded 19,849 times and has 1 formal review.

Full narrative

Sterile Insect Technique by V. A. Dyck, J. Hendrichs and A. S. Robinson was published by Taylor & Francis in 2021. Conceptually, the work connects to Insect, Sterile insect technique, Biology, Botany and PEST analysis.

OpenAlex records 382 citations. That places it in the top 1% of works in its field and year of publication. Citations peaked in 2025 with 87 citing works. Notable citing venues include Insects, bioRxiv (Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory) and Journal of Economic Entomology. Of 228 citation statements scite has classified, 3 support its claims, 222 mention it in passing, and none contradict it. The citing works include 308 journal articles, 44 preprints, 14 book chapters and 4 reviews. They come from 40 countries, led by the United States, Austria and Italy. The citation record includes 1 formal book review.

It has been downloaded 19,849 times via OAPEN. Open Library reports a combined count of 7 reading logs and catalog editions.

The latest English Wikipedia check verified 7 article–work reference matches. These are references or bibliography entries, which may include other editions of the same work; they do not measure readership.
